formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the owner's USDT0 allowance for the spender to exactly `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (`_approve(owner, spender, value)`).
Uses up the owner's current permit nonce (`nonces[owner]++`).
The signature works until `deadline`; a deadline of 0 means it never expires (`deadline == 0 || now <= deadline`).
Anyone who holds the signature can submit it. No tokens move until the spender calls transferFrom.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens" with the spender as a raw address, the max spending amount in the token (or "Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), a "Valid until" date and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit descriptor binds to domain name "Tether USD", but the contract signs under domain name "USDT0" with a salt.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json context.eip712.domain: {"name": "Tether USD", "version": "1"}. UChildUSDT0.upgradeToUSDT0 sets the name with `_setDomainSeperator("USDT0");`. EIP712Base._setDomainSeperator hashes `EIP712_DOMAIN_TYPEHASH = keccak256("EIP712Domain(string name,string version,address verifyingContract,bytes32 salt)")` with `keccak256(bytes(name))` and `bytes32(getChainId())` as the salt. UChildUSDT0.permit checks the signature against this `domainSeperator`. The code never sets the name "Tether USD", and the older UChildERC20 implementation had no permit function.
findings.fix: Set context.eip712.domain.name to the domain name the deployed contract uses ("USDT0", per upgradeToUSDT0). Check it on chain against DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(). Leave out chainId, or match the salt-based domain the contract uses.

findings.title: Permit shows deadline 0 as a 1970 date, but the code treats 0 as never expiring.
findings.evidence: UChildUSDT0.permit: `require(deadline == 0 || now <= deadline, "USDT0: PERMIT-EXPIRED");`. descriptor field `deadline` 'Valid until', format date, encoding timestamp, with no special value for 0.
findings.fix: Show deadline 0 as "No expiry", for example with a threshold-style message or a label, and add a test case with deadline 0.

findings.title: Permit intent is generic and does not name the spender or the amount being approved.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent "Authorize spending of tokens"; interpolatedIntent null. The effect is _approve(owner, spender, value) on USDT0.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Allow {spender} to spend {value}".

findings.title: Permit format has no test case, so the domain and the Unlimited/expiry renderings are never checked.
findings.fix: Add EIP-712 test messages with the real domain: one with a finite value and deadline, one with an unlimited value and one with deadline 0.
